title: The Levi M in B(Σ)_x = K_x · B(M)
body_html:
The Levi $M$ in $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$

This node clarifies Step C.7 of Plan: identify each connected component of B(Σ) as K_x · A: what is the Levi $M$ appearing in The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A's identification $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$?

What $M$ is — two layers

Abstract setup (Sheaf7 §4, line 2853)

In the abstract framework, $M \subseteq G$ is a Levi subgroup of $G$, fixed up front, together with a hypothesis (K4) relating $M$ and the $K$-cosheaf:

(K4) For every facet $\mathcal F$ of $\BSigma$, the natural inclusion $\hat M_\mathcal F \hookrightarrow \hat K_\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism $$\hat M_\mathcal F / M_{\mathcal F, 0+} \;\cong\; \hat K_\mathcal F / K_{\mathcal F, 0+}.$$

This says: the Levi quotient of the stabiliser $\hat K_\mathcal F$ (modulo its pro-unipotent radical) coincides with the corresponding quotient for $M$.

Concrete application (Sheaf7 §9, line 3348)

In the classical groups application, $M$ is specialised to be $$M \;:=\; G^\beta \;=\; \text{centraliser in } G \text{ of a semisimple element } \beta.$$

Equivalently, $M$ is the Levi attached to the orbit of $\beta$, which makes $\mathcal{B}(M)$ the Bruhat–Tits building of the Levi factor of the relevant Bushnell–Kutzko / Yu / Stevens type. The character $\phi$ in the compatible system $\Phi = (\sK_+, \phi)$ is naturally adapted to $M$.

Determined by: in the abstract setup, $M$ is part of the data (chosen alongside $K, \Phi$); in the concrete §9 setup, $M$ is determined by $\beta$ (or equivalently by the semisimple character). It is not determined by $x$ alone — but the apartment of $\BSigma$ that we choose to contain $x$ does naturally fit inside $\mathcal{B}(M)$.

The embedding $\mathcal{B}(M) \hookrightarrow \BSigma$

Choose a maximal split torus $T \subseteq M$. Since $M$ is a Levi of $G$, $T$ is also (the maximal split part of) a maximal torus of $G$.

  • $A_M := X_*(T)_M \otimes \mathbb R$ = apartment of $\mathcal{B}(M)$ attached to $T$.
  • $A := X_*(T) \otimes \mathbb R \supseteq A_M$ = apartment of $\BSigma$ attached to $T$ (the standard apartment of the generalised building).

So $A_M \subseteq A$ as Euclidean affine spaces, and the polysimplicial structure of $A_M$ refines that of $A$ (or coincides, depending on choices).

The full embedding $\mathcal{B}(M) \hookrightarrow \BSigma$ is the $M$-equivariant extension of $A_M \hookrightarrow A$: $$\mathcal{B}(M) \;=\; M \cdot A_M \;\hookrightarrow\; G \cdot A \;=\; \BSigma.$$

This is well-defined because $M \subseteq G$ acts on $\BSigma$ via the restriction of the $G$-action, and on $\mathcal{B}(M)$ via its own BT building action.

The identity $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$

Combining with The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A's $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot A$:

Lemma. $K_x \cdot A = K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$ for $x \in A_M \subseteq A$.

Proof sketch.

$\mathcal{B}(M) = M_x \cdot A_M$ (BT (A1) for $\mathcal{B}(M)$: apartments of $M$ through $x$ cover $\mathcal{B}(M)$, and $M_x$ acts transitively on these). So $K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M) = K_x M_x A_M$.

Since $A_M \subseteq A$ and $K_x M_x \subseteq \hat K_x$ (both fix $x$ in $\BSigma$), we have $K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M) \subseteq \hat K_x \cdot A = K_x \cdot A$ (The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A).

For the reverse inclusion: a point in $K_x \cdot A$ is $k \cdot a$ for $k \in K_x$, $a \in A$. Since $A = $ a single apartment containing $x$, and $\mathcal{B}(M)$ contains $A_M \subseteq A$ (in particular contains a neighborhood of $x$ in $A$ if $x \in A_M^\circ$ — and otherwise extends via $M$-translates), suitable manipulation gives $a \in M_x A_M$ (the standard apartment swap in $\mathcal{B}(M)$), hence $k \cdot a \in K_x M_x A_M = K_x \mathcal{B}(M)$.

The final equality $K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$ follows from the same conjugation argument as in The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A: $\hat K_x = K_x \cdot \Fix_N(x)$ and $\Fix_N(x) \cdot M_x \subseteq M_x \cdot \Fix_N(x)$ etc.

$\square$

Caveat. A fully rigorous proof requires (K4) and additional compatibility hypotheses between $M$ and the $K$-cosheaf. The argument above is for the typical setup where everything is built coherently around a fixed torus $T$.

Three equivalent descriptions of $C_0$ — recap

From [[node:building.component_is_KxA]]:

Description Used for
$C_0 = K_x \cdot A$ Geometric: apartments + $K$-structure
$C_0 = J \cdot A$ Algebraic: $G$-coset / $\pi_0$ structure
$C_0 = K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}(M)$ Levi-theoretic: depth-zero reduction to $M$

The Levi description is what makes the §8 reduction to depth-zero work: the $\phi$-isotypic component reduces to a problem on $M$ via $\mathcal{B}(M)$, which lives inside the $K_x \cdot$-puffed-up component $C_0$ of $\BSigma$.
